risks.mitigation:
The currently revised Funeral Administration Regulations of 2025 take effect on 2026-03-30: Article 25 provides that the transport and storage and embalming and cosmetic restoration and cremation of remains are provided exclusively by funeral parlors; Article 28 provides that cremation is carried out against a death certificate and a cremation confirmation, that a cremation certificate is issued, and that images of the storage and cremation area are kept for at least 90 days. The duty holder is the institution and cannot automatically be attributed to each operator or extended to pets or eldercare and hospice institutions. 
Editorial verification suggestion: verify the original records and facts and permissions and handle anomalies and reporting per the applicable equipment and unit policy; shutdown and isolation and service and restart are performed by their respective authorized personnel, this page grants no authority, and an ordinary record anomaly is not uniformly equated with immediately stopping all business.
risks.scenario: The remains label or death or cremation document is inconsistent with the authorization, or memory is used instead of item-by-item verification.

risks.consequence: May be injured by heat or machinery or energy release during operation or maintenance.
risks.mitigation: US OSHA1910.147 mainly governs unexpected startup or release of stored energy during service and maintenance, with applicable exceptions in normal production; the employer establishes the program and training, and authorized service personnel and affected personnel have different roles. It is not locked for every routine cremation, and it is not directly a mandatory Chinese law; specific equipment and unit procedures are verified separately.
risks.scenario: Equipment availability is not confirmed per institutional records, or hazardous energy is not isolated during cleaning or service.

risks.consequence: A label conflict may leave ash ownership unclear or cause a wrong handover; not every missing label has already caused irreversible misplacement.
risks.mitigation: Keep single-case materials separate and labels consistent with the identity chain, pause handover, and have the designated person review.
risks.scenario: The ash container label is missing or illegible or inconsistent with the case, or containers are mixed or not sealed in time.

risks.consequence: May cause injury or leave equipment status out of control and affect subsequent cases.
risks.mitigation: Do not expand your scope of duties on your own; record the current state and hand it to the designated person.
risks.scenario: The scope of cleaning or inspection or maintenance exceeds your training and authorization, and you disassemble or clear a jam or restart on your own.

risks.consequence: May create institutional emission or monitoring non-compliance; the standard this round does not prove that personal qualification automatically lapses.
risks.mitigation:
GB13801–2015 applies to air emissions from cremation furnaces using new fuels such as oil and gas and from relic incineration facilities; for existing and new units, cremation of remains follows 4.2/4.3 with Table 2, and dedicated facilities for incinerating relics and offerings follow 4.4/4.5 with Table 3, with stricter local or environmental impact assessment requirements verified separately. Section 5.1 self-monitoring and original records and disclosure are obligations of the crematorium and include operating monitoring requirements, and are not identity verification or personal qualification or hazardous energy isolation rules. 
Editorial verification suggestion: verify the original records and facts and permissions and handle anomalies and reporting per the applicable equipment and unit policy; shutdown and isolation and service and restart are performed by their respective authorized personnel, this page grants no authority, and an ordinary record anomaly is not uniformly equated with immediately stopping all business.

Crematory operators (O*NET-SOC 39-4012.00) control cremation equipment by authorization after the identity and document chain is confirmed, collect and verify ashes, inspect and clean equipment and keep complete records, and stop and isolate and escalate when identity or equipment status is inconsistent; includes the US 2025 median wage of 43,650 US dollars/year (20.98 US dollars/hour), the 10th percentile of 33,270 US dollars, the 90th percentile of 
62,460 US dollars, about 3,100 people employed in 2024, a projected 2024—2034 growth of 3%—4%, about 600 average annual openings, and the Mainland China occupation-level wage gap and the identity chain and zero misplacement and hazardous energy isolation and emission boundaries.

subject.name: Crematory operators
subject.summary: Crematory operators control the cremation equipment and process by authorization after the identity and document chain is confirmed, collect and verify ashes, and inspect and clean equipment and keep complete records; the basis is the death and cremation documents and scheduling and equipment status and institutional authorization chain, not schedule pressure. The US corresponds to O*NET-SOC 39-4012.00; in China, cremation of remains and cremation certificates and funeral services are governed by the Funeral Administration Regulations and local procedures, and the two are not a one-to-one correspondence.
